definition: The warmth of the sun in winter; the particular comfort felt when sunlight falls on the skin during cold weather.
etymology: From Latin apricus, meaning exposed to the sun or sun-warmed, itself related to aperire, to open — as if the sun opens itself to you on a cold day. The word appears in Henry Cockeram's English dictionary of 1623, one of the earliest attempts to collect the language's finer curiosities, then drifted quietly out of use, leaving a gap exactly its own shape.
usage: November offers apricity in small doses — a south-facing bench, twenty minutes around noon, the cold still present in the shadows just beyond your feet.
